subject: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stratagem.ai>, ops@stratagem.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up

Hi Elena / Stratagem ops team,

We want to let you know that between 07:45 and 08:10 PST this morning we observed a service-level issue affecting hosted text generation responses for a subset of requests (impacting about 0.9% of requests to the gen endpoint). Symptoms included partial duplicated segments and occasional sentence re-ordering — we’re calling this a "generation consistency interruption."

What we know so far:
- Root symptom: an intermittent kernel mismatch during live model hot-swap that caused a small percentage of in-flight generations to run on a variant with an incompatible sampling state.
- Impact window: 2028-12-03 07:45:12–08:09:58 PST.
- Customer-visible: elevated partial/duplicated tokens, rare truncations; no user data was lost or persisted to logs beyond normal telemetry.

Immediate actions we took:
- Scoped the affected serving pool and disabled the automated hot-swap while we investigated.
- Deployed a rolling rollback to the prior model variant by 08:12 PST for 100% mitigation.
- Flagged all affected requests for post-incident analysis and captured runtime traces/kv cache snapshots.

What we’re doing next:
- Deep postmortem and kernel selection fix; ETA for draft postmortem: 2028-12-05 EOD PST.
- Proactively identifying affected customer request IDs and will provide a summary for your ops team.
- We will post a full incident note and a status update to our status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/8271

Short-term ask from you: if you have examples of anomalous responses (request IDs, example generations), please reply and we’ll prioritize them in the analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll follow up with the postmortem and proposed remediation steps.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-8271-snapshot.txt (runtime traces + sample request IDs)

From: Elena Rossi <elena@stratagem.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, ops@stratagem.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up

Thanks for the heads up, Jordan.

A couple of quick questions from our side:
1) How confident are you that user prompts/inputs were never exposed to other tenants? We need to confirm isolation guarantees for regulatory reasons.
2) Can you confirm whether this falls under your SLO/credit policy? Our ops lead is asking if we should expect any automatic service credits for the impacted window.
3) We’ll pull request IDs now but will also need a short summary we can share with our internal stakeholders (one‑pager).

FWIW we saw about a 2.5% increase in post-generation anomaly flags in our quality monitors during that window. We’ll attach a couple of example responses once available.

- Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops, Stratagem AI
elena@stratagem.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-04T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up

Internal notes / draft reply below — keeping this in-thread for audit: 

-----Original Message-----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stratagem.ai>
Date: 2028-12-03T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up

[see above] 

DRAFT reply to Elena / Stratagem: 
- Isolation: kernel mismatch is an execution-state issue; it did not change any multi-tenant memory boundaries or storage. No customer prompts or partial outputs were written to other tenants. Security has validated memory isolation; we should attach the security note.
- Credits/SLO: per our SLO policy, isolated transient degradations that are resolved within 30 minutes do not automatically trigger credits. That said, because this produced customer-visible incorrect generations we should offer a discretionary billing credit for the impacted minute window and include it in the postmortem. Recommend: 10% credit for the hourly billing period including the incident, with AC approval.
- Deliverables: one-page summary for Stratagem ops + list of request IDs + final postmortem (PDF).

Action items for this thread: 
1) Marissa — confirm commercial credit approval path and estimate by EOD 12/04.
2) Sean — security confirmation that isolation guarantees are documented and attach short signed note.
3) Lauren — help author one-pager and coordinate the postmortem upload.

Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stratagem.ai>, ops@stratagem.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API: generation consistency interruption and follow-up — incident resolved and postmortem

Hi Elena / Stratagem ops,

Thanks for your patience — final update from our team: the incident is resolved and we’ve completed the customer-facing postmortem. Key points below and the full PDF is attached.

Summary:
- Incident ID: 8271 (https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/8271)
- Impact window: 2028-12-03 07:45:12–08:09:58 PST
- Impact: ~0.9% of gen requests served anomalous token sequences (duplication/reordering/truncation).
- Root cause: during an automated model variant hot-swap, an edge kernel selection path invoked a variant with incompatible RNG/sampling state for a small subset of in-flight requests.
- Data exposure: NO. Security validation attached (signed) confirms no cross-tenant memory or storage contamination.

Remediations implemented:
- Disabled automated hot-swap kernels pending a compatibility check.
- Added runtime assertion to detect sampling-state mismatches and fail-safe to fallback variant early.
- CI regression test added to exercise kernel selection during variant swaps.

Compensation and next steps:
- Commercial: We’ve approved a discretionary 10% credit for the affected hour; Marissa will follow up with an accounting note and invoice adjustment.
- Postmortem: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/file/d/pm-8271 (PDF attached: postmortem-8271.pdf)
- We’ll host a 30-minute technical walk-through with your ML infra team if you’d like — propose 2028-12-07 10:00 PST or 2028-12-08 13:00 PST.

Please let us know preferred time for the walk-through and if you need any additional artifacts (request IDs, diffs, or sanitized traces).

Apologies again for the interruption. We appreciate the partnership and will keep you updated on the longer-term kernel-selection hardening roadmap.

Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-8271.pdf
